proposal.summary: Preserve existing discovery and PDF guidance. Clarify review scope and add a memory preventing evidence loss during later extraction.

edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Give extraction and review calls the same field definition, temporal scope, and inclusion rules. When the task calls for affiliations recorded in an award announcement, review completeness against that announcement rather than expanding to every outside appointment in a biography. Resolve review findings against the task scope before launching further research. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads.

edits.title: Prevent later extractions from discarding supported facts
edits.content: A later nationality extraction replaced a validated multi-country value with a single-country mention from another person's page. Schema and quote-membership checks passed; the loss was caught only by comparing with the earlier evidence. Before replacing a populated cell, provide the existing value and supporting evidence alongside new evidence, then compare the proposed change for lost facts. A source mentioning only one component does not disprove other supported components, and a failed corroborating fetch does not invalidate existing evidence. Retain the earlier cell unless stronger evidence justifies the change; resolve genuine conflicts explicitly. Validate proposed replacements before mutating accumulated records.

additional_candidates.description: Broad audit prompts generated out-of-scope affiliation investigations; explicit field definitions restored focused review.
A later extraction discarded supported nationalities despite passing structural and quotation checks; comparison with earlier evidence recovered them.
A noncontiguous PDF quotation was repaired using an exact slice of stored text.

decisions.reason: All 34 occurrences were considered. Signals 0–6 correspond to seven annual searches whose inspected snippets contained no laureate names; signals 7–31 cover 25 nationality searches for already identified people; signals 32–33 cover two verification searches for known people. These searches supplied useful sources despite adding no new entities. The trajectory records inspected results and honest empty discoveries, rather than premature placeholders. Entry 0 already explicitly permits this behavior. Its single successful outcome with these signals does not establish consistently bad guidance or warrant suppressing legitimate empty records.

Signal 34 records a Princeton HTTP 403, recovered through an already discovered Lindau source. Signal 35 records a TAP certificate failure during corroboration; previously fetched MIT evidence remained available and was ultimately retained. Neither failure caused repeated download attempts or unsupported use of the failed page. These isolated backend failures do not justify host-specific rules. The consequential evidence-replacement regression is addressed separately.

Annual audit responses proposed investigating outside advisory and undated appointments after the extraction had been scoped to official award announcements. The root restated that scope, repaired actual announcement omissions, and obtained a focused final PASS. Entry 2 already covers affiliation distinctions, so a narrow update preserves this successful recovery without creating a duplicate skill or imposing the announcement-only definition on unrelated tasks.

The resolution call received only newly fetched evidence and replaced an existing three-country nationality with a one-country navigation-table mention. Its quotation existed verbatim and structural checks reported no cell errors. The next root turn recognized the lost support and restored the earlier person-specific evidence. Final citation success therefore does not erase this recovered failure. Existing entries address missing fields and quotation repair, but not semantic regression when overwriting populated cells.

The initial affiliation quote substituted the wrong interleaved PDF line. The root located the relevant stored passage, copied a contiguous slice, and rechecked membership; final citations passed. Entry 1 already describes this exact failure and completed repair procedure. Its recorded successful outcome supports retention without another edit.
